column1: For the first century or so of the industrial revolution, increased productivity led to decreases in working hours.
column2: 在工业革命开始后大约一个世纪的时间里，生产率的提高带来了工作时间的缩短。
column3: first century or so|最初约一个世纪
column5: increased productivity|n. 生产率的提高

column1: Employees who had been putting in 12-hour days, six days a week, found their time on the job shrinking to 10 hours daily, then finally to eight hours, five days a week.
column2: 那些过去每周工作六天、每天工作12小时的员工发现，他们的工作时间逐渐减少：从每天12小时降至10小时，最终变为每周五天、每天8小时。

column1: Only a generation ago social planners worried about what people would do with all this new-found free time.
column2: 就在一代人之前，社会规划者还担心人们会如何利用这些新获得的空闲时间。

column1: In the US, at least it seems they need not have bothered.
column2: 在美国，至少看起来他们根本不必为此担忧。

column1: Although the output per hour of work has more than doubled since 1945, leisure seems reserved largely for the unemployed and underemployed.
column2: 尽管自1945年以来每小时工作产出已翻倍以上，但休闲时间似乎仍主要被失业者和就业不足的人所占据。

column1: Those who work full-time spend as much time on the job as they did at the end of World War II.
column2: 全职工作者花在工作上的时间，与二战结束时一样多。

column1: In fact, working hours have increased noticeably since 1970 — perhaps because real wages have stagnated since that year.
column2: 事实上，从1970年起，工时明显延长了——这或许是因为实际工资从那一年起就停滞不前。

column1: Bookstores now abound with manuals describing how to manage time and cope with stress.
column2: 现在的书店里到处都是关于如何管理时间和应对压力的指南书籍。

column1: There are several reasons for lost leisure.
column2: 人们的闲暇时间减少，有好几个原因。
column5: lost leisure|n. 减少的闲暇时间

column1: Since 1979, companies have responded to improvements in the business climate by having employees work overtime rather than by hiring extra personnel, says economist Juliet B. Schor of Harvard University.
column2: 自1979年以来，商业环境好转时，企业的应对方式一直是让员工加班，而非增聘人手。这是哈佛大学经济学家朱丽叶·B·肖尔的观察。

column1: Indeed, the current economic recovery has gained a certain amount of notoriety for its “jobless” nature: increased production has been almost entirely decoupled from employment.
column2: 事实上，当前经济复苏因其‘失业’特性而广受关注：生产增长几乎完全与就业无关。

column1: Some firms are even downsizing as their profits climb.
column2: 一些公司甚至在利润上升的同时进行裁员。

column1: “All things being equal, we’d be better off spreading around the work,” observes labour economist Ronald G. Ehrenberg of Cornell University.
column2: 康奈尔大学的劳动经济学家罗纳德·G·埃伦伯格指出：‘在其他条件相同的情况下，我们应当将工作更均匀地分配给更多人。’

column1: Yet a host of factors pushes employers to hire fewer workers for more hours and at the same time compels workers to spend more time on the job.
column2: 然而，诸多因素促使雇主减少雇员数量、增加工作时长，同时迫使员工在工作岗位上投入更多时间。

column1: Most of those incentives involve what Ehrenberg calls the structure of compensation: quirks in the way salaries and benefits are organised that make it more profitable to ask 40 employees to labour an extra hour each than to hire one more worker to do the same 40-hour job.
column2: 这些激励措施中的大多数都涉及埃伦伯格所说的薪酬结构：即薪资和福利安排中的某些特点，使得让40名员工每人多工作一小时，比雇佣一名新员工完成同样的40小时工作更划算。

column1: Professional and managerial employees supply the most obvious lesson along these lines.
column2: 专业和管理类员工提供了最明显的教训。

column1: Once people are on salary, their cost to a firm is the same whether they spend 35 hours a week in the office or 70.
column2: 一旦员工开始领取薪水，他们对公司的成本无论是在办公室工作35小时还是70小时都是一样的。

column1: Diminishing returns may eventually set in as overworked employees lose efficiency or leave for more arable pastures.
column2: 员工工作过度，效率会下降，也有人会另谋更好的出路。这样一来，边际收益最终可能开始递减。
column6: overworked employees|n. 过度劳累的员工
column8: more arable pastures|更好的发展机会

column1: But in the short run, the employer’s incentive is clear.
column2: 但短期内，雇主的激励是明确的。

column1: Even hourly employees receive benefits – such as pension contributions and medical insurance – that are not tied to the number of hours they work.
column2: 即使是按小时计酬的员工，也能获得养老金缴纳和医疗保险等福利，这些福利并不与他们工作时长挂钩。

column1: Therefore, it is more profitable for employers to work their existing employees harder.
column2: 因此，对雇主而言，让现有员工更努力工作更合算。

column1: For all that employees complain about long hours, they too have reasons not to trade money for leisure.
column2: 尽管员工抱怨工作时间长，他们也有不愿用金钱换取闲暇的理由。

column1: “People who work reduced hours pay a huge penalty in career terms,” Schor maintains.
column2: “缩短工作时间的人会在职业发展上付出很大的代价，”肖尔坚持认为。
column4: pay a huge penalty|付出很大的代价
column5: in career terms|在职业发展方面

column1: “It’s taken as a negative signal’ about their commitment to the firm.’
column2: 这被视为他们对公司承诺的负面信号。

column1: [Lotte] Bailyn [of Massachusetts Institute of Technology] adds that many corporate managers find it difficult to measure the contribution of their underlings to a firm’s well-being, so they use the number of hours worked as a proxy for output.
column2: 麻省理工学院的洛特·贝林补充说，许多企业管理者觉得，很难衡量下属对企业良好经营所作的贡献，于是就用工时来间接衡量产出。
column7: firm’s well-being|企业的良好经营状况
column9: proxy for|n. 间接衡量……的指标

column1: “Employees know this,” she says, and they adjust their behavior accordingly.
column2: ‘员工们都知道这一点，’她说，因此他们会相应地调整自己的行为。

column1: “Although the image of the good worker is the one whose life belongs to the company,” Bailyn says, “it doesn’t fit the facts.”
column2: “人们心目中的好员工，整个人生都属于公司，”贝林说，“可这种形象与事实并不相符。”
column4: image|n. 人们心目中的形象

column1: She cites both quantitative and qualitative studies that show increased productivity for part-time workers: they make better use of the time they have and they are less likely to succumb to fatigue in stressful jobs.
column2: 她援引了定量和定性两类研究，这些研究都表明，兼职员工的工作效率有所提高。他们更能充分利用工作时间，在压力大的岗位上也较少会因疲劳而撑不住。
column8: make better use of|更充分地利用
column12: stressful jobs|n. 压力大的工作

column1: Companies that employ more workers for less time also gain from the resulting redundancy, she asserts.
column2: 她断言，企业多雇一些员工，让每人少工作一些时间，还能从由此形成的人员余量中获益。
column4: for less time|工作时间较短
column7: redundancy|n. 可供调配的人员余量

column1: “The extra people can cover the contingencies that you know are going to happen, such as when crises take people away from the workplace.”
column2: “多一些人可以应对那些注定会发生的情况，比如危机导致人员离开工作岗位。”,

column1: Positive experiences with reduced hours have begun to change the more-is-better culture at some companies, Schor reports.
column2: 据Schor报道，一些公司正在改变‘多就好’的文化。

column1: Larger firms, in particular, appear to be more willing to experiment with flexible working arrangements…
column2: 尤其是规模较大的企业，似乎更愿意尝试灵活的工作安排……

column1: It may take even more than changes in the financial and cultural structures of employment for workers successfully to trade increased productivity and money for leisure time, Schor contends.
column2: 肖尔认为，劳动者若想把更高的生产率和收入换成闲暇时间，光改变就业制度的经济结构和文化结构可能还不够。
column9: increased productivity|n. 提高的生产率

column1: She says the U.S. market for goods has become skewed by the assumption of full-time, two-career households.
column2: 她说，美国商品市场出现了偏差，因为它把双方都全职工作的双职工家庭视为常态。
column3: market for goods|n. 商品市场

column1: Automobile makers no longer manufacture cheap models, and developers do not build the tiny bungalows that served the first postwar generation of home buyers.
column2: 汽车制造商已经不再生产廉价车型，房地产开发商也不再建造那种曾满足战后第一代购房者需求的小平房。

column1: Not even the humblest household object is made without a microprocessor.
column2: 就连最普通的家用物品，其制造过程中也都会用到微处理器。

column1: As Schor notes, the situation is a curious inversion of the “appropriate technology” vision that designers have had for developing countries: U.S. goods are appropriate only for high incomes and long hours.
column2: 正如肖尔所说，这种局面颇为奇特：它把设计者为发展中国家设想的“适用技术”理念颠倒了过来。美国的商品只适合收入高、工作时间长的人。
